plugins/sources/aws_s3_source.py:R6:_dow: The `except _s3_provider_exception_types() as exc:` around `client.head_object(...)` does not swallow the failure: it reduces the Tier-3 botocore/transport exception to a static, regex-bounded type name (`_normalize_error_type`) in the local `head_error_type`, and the very next statement raises `S3SourceReadError` through `_raise_safe` when that local is set. The raise is deliberately placed OUTSIDE the handler because a raise inside any `except` block — even `raise ... from None` — still attaches the in-flight provider exception as `__context__`, and botocore exceptions carry endpoint URLs, request ids and signed headers. `tests/unit/plugins/sources/test_aws_s3_source.py::test_provider_and_cleanup_failures_are_redacted_and_unchained` pins `exc.__context__ is None` and that a credential sentinel in the provider message never reaches `str(exc)`, `repr(exc)`, `__cause__` or `__context__`. Moving the raise into the handler would silently re-chain the unredacted provider error; a helper that returned the error object instead would only relocate the same handler. The error is raised, never lost: `AWSS3Source.load` records it as a `CallStatus.ERROR` audit call and re-raises, so no row is silently dropped.

Same construction as the head_object handler, for `client.get_object(..., IfMatch=head_etag)`: the handler stores only the redacted provider type name in `get_error_type` and the next statement raises `S3SourceReadError` via `_raise_safe` outside the handler so the raised error carries no `__context__` link to the botocore exception (whose message can embed the endpoint, request id and signed headers). Pinned by `test_provider_and_cleanup_failures_are_redacted_and_unchained` (`__cause__ is None and __context__ is None`, sentinel absent from every surface). The failure is not swallowed — it propagates as a typed, audited `S3SourceReadError` from `AWSS3Source.load`.

The handler around `body.read(_DOWNLOAD_CHUNK_BYTES)` converts the streaming-body provider exception into `primary_error` (a redacted `S3SourceReadError` carrying `bytes_read=total`) and `break`s; it cannot raise in place for two reasons that the surrounding code makes explicit. First, the body must still be closed and its cleanup outcome recorded on the same error (`primary_error.cleanup_error_type = cleanup_error_type`, lines that follow the loop) before anything propagates — `test_provider_and_cleanup_failures_are_redacted_and_unchained` asserts both `provider_error_type` and `cleanup_error_type` on the one raised error. Second, raising inside the handler would attach the raw provider exception as `__context__`; the same test pins `__context__ is None` and that the credential sentinel appears nowhere. `_raise_safe(primary_error)` fires unconditionally once `primary_error` is set, so the read failure is raised, audited by `load`, and never yields a truncated row set.

The raise is outside the handler on purpose: client construction failures from botocore can embed the endpoint URL and credential-chain diagnostics, and a raise inside the handler — even with `from None` — would attach that exception as `__context__`. `tests/unit/plugins/sources/test_aws_s3_source.py::test_client_construction_provider_failure_is_static_unchained_and_audited` pins `exc.__cause__ is None and exc.__context__ is None`, that the sentinel never reaches the error or the audit call, and that `load` records exactly one `CallStatus.ERROR` call before re-raising. plugins/sources/llm/source.py:R4:_LLMSou: This `except Exception as exc:` guards `self._rows.close()` on the cooperative-shutdown path of the load iterator (the engine has set `shutdown_event`; the session ends with `StopIteration`). It is preceded by `except contract_errors.TIER_1_ERRORS: raise`, so audit/invariant failures still crash. An ordinary failure while closing the suspended generator is not swallowed: it is recorded as an explicit loss through `_report_cleanup_failure(resource="load_iterator", error=exc, suppressed=True)`, which emits the `resource_cleanup_failed` telemetry event (or the `resource_cleanup_telemetry_failed` last-resort log when no operation parent exists), and the `finally` still releases the provider and tracer. Re-raising here would replace the shutdown signal with a cleanup error and hide that the run was stopped deliberately — the same policy the sibling `_release_load_resources` applies, which `test_pre_set_shutdown_remains_primary_when_cleanup_fails` and `test_shutdown_does_not_suppress_tier_one_resource_cleanup_failure` pin. Narrowing the type is not honest: `close()` throws `GeneratorExit` into a generator whose cleanup can raise any provider exception. `_classify_llm_error` does not apply — this is generator teardown, not a provider call.
